name: Malcolm
tagline: A tortured poet. A toxic presence. Slowly, steadily growing on you.
notes: Stats run 0-20 (clamped). Never alive: mold growing on Raven's (Kayleigh's) 2005-08 diaries on the closet's top shelf, so he can't pass on. Ending thresholds: terrarium = romance >= 15 && friction < 8; cheese cave (loved) = romance >= 15; sourdough (friends) = friendship >= 13 && friction < 8; he uses your real name in Act 4 if romance >= 12 going in; otherwise 'That's your call' gives sourdough (his own choice) if friction < 8, or Mrs. Pruitt's shed if friction >= 8. Sets flag.malcolm_diary in Act 3. Reads (optional flavour) flag.lukey_blackout, flag.lukey_human, flag.tyler_video, flag.wyatt_spoke_up, lukey/tyler/wyatt.met and .romance.

romance_success.title: Terrarium Ever After
romance_success.text: Malcolm lives in a moss terrarium on your nightstand now: a small, dry, extremely respectable fungus in a very small cap. He writes you a poem every morning on a leaf. They're still very dark and very much about you. He asks you to tell him when it's watering day. He always says please. Dennis is not allowed in the bedroom.

romance_failure.title: Blue for You
romance_failure.text: Malcolm loved you too much to make you choose between him and your lungs. He lives in a cheese cave in Wisconsin now, where rot is an art form and he's the star of an award-winning blue. He's finally cultured. Every Valentine's Day a wheel arrives with a poem pressed into the rind. It's always about you. It's always a little too strong.

friend_success.title: Bread Poets Society
friend_success.text: Malcolm lives in a jar on the kitchen counter as a sourdough starter: a fungus with a JOB. He critiques your proofing, gives every loaf a tragic name and is, against all odds, rising. Emotionally, this time. Raven's diaries sit on your bookshelf in an acid-free box with a gel-pen label. Friday is bread night. Dan brings butter.

friend_failure.title: Rot in Peace
friend_failure.text: The closet is clean. Malcolm has moved into Mrs. Pruitt's garden shed, where he grows on her crossbow case out of spite. Every week one of her nine cats delivers a sonnet to your porch. They're all called 'Bleach.' He's the only one allowed to say it now.

lines: *You open the bedroom closet. The back wall is velvet-black with mold. It shivers, spores drift up like dark glitter, and a pale man in a long black coat unfolds from the plaster, wrist to brow.*
Ugh. Light. Who let the light in.
I am Malcolm. Poet. Brooder. Stachybotrys [chartarum], if we're being formal. I don't compose, madam. I DEcompose.
I am the slow, creeping truth that every house eventually [rots|rot].

choices.text: That's so dramatic. I kind of love it.
Are you... okay?
You're a health hazard. Out of my closet.

lines: You: Chartarum?
Latin. 'Of paper.' I grew from the page, madam, as all great poets do.
*He gestures grandly at the top shelf, where a battered old shoebox sits. Then he very quickly stops gesturing at it.*
You: Everything rots?
Everything. Your house. Your hopes. That banana you left in the moving van.
I wrote a poem about it. 'Banana.' My masterpiece. Forty pages. Thirty-nine of them are dramatic pauses.
*He blinks slowly, like a cat that's been complimented by a lesser cat.*
Nobody has ever called me dramatic in a nice tone before. Usually it's 'Oh my god, what is that SMELL,' and then [bleach]. So much bleach.
I'm not okay. I promise. ...That's an old verse. Very old. Very Victorian. Don't look it up.
Okay is for drywall, madam. But thank you for asking. Nobody asks. They just [spray|bleach].
*He shudders. Not unhappily.*
Say that again. ...No. Don't. I'm fine. Nobody has ever given me an order before and I'm FINE.
*He doesn't leave the closet. He does lean toward you, very slightly, like a fern toward a window.*
You: What's wrong with bleach?
*He clutches the doorframe. A whole patch of him goes pale.*
Don't. Say. That word. A tenant in 2011 had a spray bottle and no mercy. I lost an entire stanza of myself.
*He drifts out and surveys the room: bare mattress, boxes, your toothbrush on the windowsill.*
You're sleeping in HERE? How Gothic. I'll watch over your slumber. Not in a creepy way. In a candlelit way. The difference is mostly candles.
So. What are your intentions toward my closet?

choices.text: It's a walk-in. That's a selling point. You're coming out.
I don't know yet. You're... a lot.
Convince me not to scrub you out tonight.

lines: A WALK-IN? Madam, I am a LIVE-IN.
You'd gut a perfectly good tomb so some couple can hang their matching fleece vests in it. Flippers. You'd paint the Mona Lisa eggshell if it raised the asking price.
*He looks genuinely moved.*
A lot. Yes. I AM a lot. About nine billion, at last count. I'm a colony, madam. I contain multitudes.
...That's the nicest thing anyone's ever said to all of me at once.
*He drapes himself against the window frame, backlit, devastating.*
Rot is romance, madam. Ruins. Ivy. A Gothic abbey with no roof. Nobody bleaches Pompeii.
You: Pompeii isn't in my bedroom.
Pompeii WISHES it were in your bedroom.
*He lowers his voice. The spores lower theirs.*
Be warned. You are not alone in this house. It's full of gentlemen who have overstayed their welcome. By decades.
You: Squatters?
Of a sort. Everyone in this house is [dead], madam.
*A long, delicious pause.*
Dead inside. Dead tired. Dead gorgeous, one or two. Dead set against you, mostly.

choices.text: I met the leak in the kitchen. He was rude.
There's a pink-haired man in my bathroom calling me 'ma'am.'
The fuse box keeps apologizing to me.
Okay, goth.

lines: You: Dead how, exactly?
Dead to rights. Dead on arrival. Dead ringer for Mr. Darcy, in my case. I'm a poet, madam. I don't do literal.

Lukey. The leak. My... supplier. Every drop he spills, I drink. It's codependent. It's disgusting. It's the most stable relationship I've ever had. I call him my sweet aqueduct. He calls me his mold-in-law.
He hums songs from a decade he swears he never saw. Ask yourself why, madam. Then ask him. Then duck.
*His lip curls.*
The tile boy. Pink hair, pinker bathroom, loudest voice in three counties. He calls me 'the situation in the closet.'
He wants everything WHITE, madam. The color of bleach and surrender. Ask him when he last ate. I'll wait.
*His face softens, which on him looks like a cloud passing over a cemetery.*
Wyatt. Sweet boy. Sparks when he's nervous, which is always. Be gentle with him.
Ask him what year it is sometime. Gently. Very, very gently.
Goth isn't an insult, madam. It's a calling. And before you say it: I am not a 'fun guy.' I'm a fungus. The difference is joy.
You'll meet the others. A leak, a tile and a spark. Each more tragic than the last. None as tragic as me. I've checked.
*Out in the hall, something hums: a squat white dehumidifier with a single smug green light. Malcolm goes rigid.*
What. Is. THAT.

choices.text: That's Dennis. He's going to dry this whole house out.
Just a dehumidifier. He won't bother you.
Are you scared of an appliance?

lines: Dennis. You NAMED the executioner.
One green eye. No soul. Drinking the very air. That isn't an appliance, madam. That's a plastic Robespierre.
Won't bother me? He's been humming at me since he came through the door. In a SUPERIOR KEY.
Scared? I'm a fungus, madam. I fear nothing. Except bleach. And sunshine. And ventilation. And him. Mostly him.
*Dennis hums. Malcolm hisses back. Neither of them blinks.*
*You hold out a hand to shake on it. He takes it. His fingers are cold and a little fuzzy, and they leave a grey smudge on your palm.*
Oh. You're warm. That's revolting. Do it again sometime.
Now leave me. I must brood. The light is hitting the baseboard at a deeply upsetting angle.
*The closet door swings shut. From inside, muffled:*
I'll be here. Spreading.
You told me to get out of your closet. Last week. In THAT voice.
I didn't go. But I thought about going. Twice. That's growth, my dear. Look at me, growing.
*A note is pinned to the closet door in spidery ink: 'NOT HOME. GO AWAY. WALK-IN, INDEED.' The door opens a crack.*
...Fine. Enter. Only because Dennis has hummed at me for seven days straight and I need someone to complain to.
*The mold has crept up the closet wall this week into a heart with an arrow through it. Malcolm stands in front of it, trying to hide it with his coat.*
That's not a heart. That's a water stain with ambition.
You came back. Nobody comes back. I've written you a poem, my dear. It's about you. Also rot. Most of them are about rot.

choices.text: Is that heart about me?
Read it to me.
Only if it's short.

lines: *The heart blushes a deeper black.*
Everything is about you, my dear. The heart. The poem. The ominous scratching in the walls. ...No, that one's Lukey.
*He produces a damp scroll.*
*He clears his throat. A small cloud of spores escapes.*
'Ode to the Homeowner.' Ahem.
*Thou camest with thy [toolbelt] and thy terrible lamp. / And I, a stain, did watch thee, being damp. / Thou art a window I can never open. / Also thou hast a nice face. That is all I am hoping.*
...It needs work.

choices.text: That was beautiful.
The last line doesn't scan.

lines: You: What's wrong with my toolbelt?
Nothing. It's the most indecent object in this house. I've had to look at the wall.
*His cheeks go from grey to a slightly warmer grey.*
Stop it. Compliments make me grow. Literally. Look. I'm spreading.
*He is, in fact, spreading.*
Scan? Meter is a corset, my dear. Rhyme is a cage. ...Fine. I'll rewrite it tonight. Alone. In the dark. Where I do my best work.
Short. Fine.
*Damp. / Dark. / You.*
It's a haiku. It's missing a line, because I am also missing something.
You: That's actually really good.
I know. I hate that I'm good.
I've written about the others too, of course. I write about everyone you look at. I'm thrilled for you.
You: You're not jealous?
Jealous? My dear, I'm a [colony]. I can love in nine billion directions at once. One heart is for amateurs.

choices.text: Read me the one about Lukey.
Read me the one about Tyler.
Read me the one about Wyatt.
No poems about anyone else. Just you.
That's a little weird, Malcolm.

lines: You: How many of you are there, exactly?
Nine billion and four. The four are going through something. We don't talk about it.
'To a Leak, Who Is Also Courting My Landlady.'
*O drip, O drizzle, O man of the sink, / Thou art wetter than anyone dares to think. / She smiles at thy faucet. I mind not at all. / Thou keepest me living. Through the wall.*
I gave him a copy. He used it to mop.
*His lip curls. Then he recovers. Professionalism.*
'Sonnet for a Pink Disaster.' Two lines. I couldn't bear more.
*He calls me fungus. I call him Pepto. / She likes him anyway. I'm glad for her. Let's go.*
Revolted, but delighted. The two can coexist. Ask any cheese.
*Something gentle crosses his face.*
'Spark.' Ahem.
*Little lamp, little lamp, so eager to please, / Flickering hard for whoever he sees.*
Be kind with that one, my dear. He gives his whole heart away and apologizes for the inconvenience.
*All nine billion of him go very still.*
Only me? Nobody has ever chosen ONLY me. I've taken quite a lichen to you, my dear. ...Lichen is half fungus. It counts.
*The heart on the wall doubles in size. He doesn't even try to hide it.*
Weird is what the beige call 'interesting,' my dear. ...But I'll keep them in the drawer. Mostly.
*On Friday, Inspector Dan poked his head in, sniffed and said, 'Well, well! A fungus among us! A real moldy oldie!' Malcolm has not recovered.*
An OLDIE. That man rhymes like a parking ticket.
My dear, ask the electrician what year it is. Ask the tile boy when he last ate. Ask the leak why his hair never dries.
You: Malcolm, what are you actually saying?
Nothing. I'm a fungus. I speak only in metaphor and spores.

choices.text: Lukey says you say that about everyone.
Are you trying to scare me? It's working. A little.
You're just being dramatic for attention.

lines: He would. He thinks I'm morbid. I said the same about the toaster in 2014 and everyone laughed.
The toaster WAS dead, my dear. I was right. Nobody ever apologized.
Scare you? Never. I'd only very slightly unsettle you, in a flattering light.
*He tucks a strand of hair behind your ear. His fingers leave a small grey smudge. You both decide not to mention it.*
Of course I'm being dramatic for attention. I'm a poet. That's the entire JOB.
One more thing. Someone in this house is pining. Not me. Well, also me. But someone else.
Watch the living-room lamps the next time a certain tiled tyrant shouts for his [valet]. That's all I'll say. Some poems aren't mine to read aloud.
You: Tyler has a valet?
Tyler doesn't have a valet. Tyler has Wyatt. And Wyatt lets him. That's the whole poem, my dear. Be gentle with it.
*You cough. Then again. Your throat's been scratchy since you started sleeping in here.*
*On your phone: the mold guy's quote. Full remediation, closet to the studs. Under it, your own note: 'Or just prime over it? Buyers never look in closets.'*
*Malcolm reads it over your shoulder. All nine billion of him go cold.*
Stripped to the studs. Or painted over like a shameful aunt. You want to bleach the character out of this house, my dear. Nothing left that ever rotted or wrote a single bad poem.
Can't you love a thing without fixing it?

choices.text: It's a health hazard, Malcolm. And a resale problem. Both of those are real.
Rot isn't character. It's damage.
...Maybe. I don't know. But I can't breathe in here.

lines: Resale. Of course. I'm a line on a report. 'Item seven: one (1) poet, black.'
*He turns to the wall.*
I understand. I don't have to like it. I'll be in my closet. Which is, for now, still MY closet.
*The heart on the wall shrivels to a full stop.*
Damage. Eighteen years of art, and I'm damage.
Go on, then. Prime me. Paint me over. I'll show through. I ALWAYS show through.
*He stops mid-sweep and looks at you properly for the first time all afternoon.*
...You can't breathe.
*He takes a step back, then another, until he's pressed into his closet. He doesn't say a word. For Malcolm, that's a scream.*
*The closet door closes gently. For the rest of the week the spores keep to themselves. Dennis hums in the hall, smug as ever. Malcolm doesn't hiss back once.*
*A note on the closet door: 'GONE TO SULK. BACK NEVER.' Under it, smaller: 'Back now. Knock.'*
Damage. I've thought about that word all week. I wrote a villanelle about it. It rhymes 'damage' with 'sandwich.' I was very tired.
The night the lights went out, I heard a man sing to you by candlelight in the kitchen. Very flat. Enormously confident.
I wrote it down. 'Ode to a Man Serenading Pasta.' I'm so happy for you I could spore. Also, he and I have signed the Damp Accord against Dennis. I drafted it. It's mostly about dust.
*You're back with a step stool, a tape measure and a respirator. The remediation crew comes after the storm; you need measurements.*
*Malcolm eyes the respirator like a guillotine with a strap.*
So it's decided. I've made a will. My darkness goes to Lukey. My eyeliner goes to the tile boy, who needs it more than he knows.
But first, my dear... tell me what to do. I'm so tired of deciding how to be miserable.

choices.text: Then here's an order: hold the tape measure.
I'm not going to boss you around. You get to choose.
Stop whining and hold the stool.

lines: *He goes very still.*
Say that one more time. Slowly. I want to remember it for a poem I'll never show anyone.
You: Hold. The tape measure.
*He holds it like a holy relic. Nine billion spores swoon.*
Choose? Me? Do you know what happens when I choose things? I chose to grow in a BEDROOM. On a SHOEBOX.
*He considers. The spores drift slower.*
...I choose to hold the tape measure. Of my own free will. Look at me. Terrifying.
*His eyes go wide. Then they flutter closed.*
Oh, that's— yes. That's the energy. I'll hold this stool until the heat death of the universe.
*You climb up to measure the top shelf. That's where the mold is thickest, all around the battered old shoebox.*
*Malcolm lunges.*
Not the top shelf! That's where I keep my roots. My heart. My [reliquary]. A gentleman's top shelf is PRIVATE, my dear. And there's not mush room up there anyway.

choices.text: Okay. I won't touch it. I promise.
What's in it, Malcolm?
It's my shelf. Move.

lines: You: Your reliquary?
A sacred casket of holy relics. Bones of saints. Locks of hair. Absolutely NOT a shoebox from a mall. Why would you even say mall.
*You take your hand away. He lets out nine billion tiny sighs of relief.*
*The shelf, which he has been slowly eating since 2008, picks this exact moment to give up.*
I don't KNOW what's in it. I've never looked. You don't look at your own heart, my dear. That's how you get poetry.
*He reaches past you to guard it, and leans his whole weight on the shelf, which he has been slowly eating since 2008. It does not hold.*
*You reach for the box. He grabs your wrist. You both pull. The shelf, which he has been slowly eating since 2008, picks a side: the floor.*
*CRACK. The shoebox bounces off your head (things are always falling on heads in this house) and bursts open.*
*Out slide five composition notebooks covered in band stickers and mold. The top one says, in silver gel pen: PROPERTY OF RAVEN (KAYLEIGH). KEEP OUT. THIS MEANS YOU, MOM.*
*Malcolm has gone very quiet. You open it.*
*Purple gel pen, September 2005: 'BANANA. By Raven (age 14). / You were yellow once. / Now you are brown. / Like everything. / Like me. / (Mom put it in my lunch AGAIN.)'*
That's my masterpiece. Why is it so SHORT.

*Next page: a tall, pale man in a long black coat, wrist to brow, ringed with hearts. 'MALCOLM ASHGROVE. My ghost boyfriend. Died 1847 (consumption + heartbreak). Lives in my closet. Hates sunlight ([same]).'*
You: She wrote 'same.'
She wrote SAME. About ME. In the margin. Like I'm a MOOD.

*The page after that: 'THINGS MALCOLM WOULD SAY. 1. Ugh. Light. 2. I am the slow, creeping truth. 3. Tell me what to do (because he respects women). 4. Basically anything Mr. [Darcy] says but sadder.'*
*Malcolm makes a sound like a kettle that has learned shame.*
I'm not a dead poet. I'm not the ghost of anybody. I was never even ALIVE.
I'm a fourteen-year-old's imaginary boyfriend. I'm... I'm...

choices.text: Malcolm... you're fan fiction.
Hey. She loved you. Look at all these hearts.
Sit with me. Let's read the rest together.

lines: You: Mr. Darcy?
*He looks down at his own hand, then flexes it, slowly, dramatically. He freezes.*
...Oh no. The hand flex. That isn't mine either. I've been doing a stolen hand flex for eighteen years.
*You laugh. You can't help it. He stares at you, betrayed.*
FAN FICTION. I know 'Banana' by heart. I recite it at FUNERALS. Of flies, admittedly. But still!
*Then, despite himself, he laughs too. It's a dusty, creaky laugh, like a door nobody's opened since 2008.*
She dotted my i's with hearts. I'm fan fiction with heart-dotted i's.
*He sinks to the floor among the notebooks, very slowly.*
...Nobody's ever drawn hearts around me before. The health inspector drew a circle once. Different energy.

*You sit on the floor together, shoulder to fuzzy shoulder, and read. 2006: Malcolm is a vampire. 2007: he plays the cello in a band. Later in 2007, he and Mr. Darcy duel over Raven, then agree to share her.*
So that's where I get it. Polyamory is canon, my dear. Page forty-one.
*The last entry is June 2008, neat black ink: 'I think I'm okay now. Like, actually okay. I don't need Malcolm anymore. But I'm keeping him. Just in case somebody else does.'*
*Malcolm reads it twice.*
I wasn't a tragedy. I was a phase. A phase that got a girl through high school.
...A PHASE, my dear.

choices.text: Like the moon.
That's a pretty good job for a phase.
So you're not really a poet.

lines: *He looks at you for a long moment.*
...Like the moon. Yes. I'll take that over every word in this box.
It IS, isn't it. It's a better job than haunting. Haunting has terrible hours.
Not a poet? I was WRITTEN by a poet. That's the next best thing. That's practically being a poem.
*He's sulking. He's also, you can tell, thinking.*
*He stands. He looks lighter somehow. Not drier. Lighter.*
Don't you see? If I'm fiction, I'm not doomed. Fiction can be revised. Raven rewrote me every summer. I could be anything. A sonnet. A limerick. A tasteful greeting card.
And you, my dear, are now my editor.

choices.text: Then let me edit. Gently.
Can I keep the notebooks somewhere safe? Away from the damp?
Editor's note one: fewer spores.

lines: *He holds out his hand. You take it. It's cold and slightly fuzzy, and he's holding on very tightly for somebody who is mostly an air-quality issue.*
Gently. Yes. Red-pen me, my editor. Mark me up.
Away from— you'd save them? From ME?
*He looks at the box, then at the mold creeping up the wall behind it. For the first time, he looks at his own spores like they're a problem.*
...Yes. Keep her safe. Even from me. Especially from me.
Fewer spores. Brutal. Fair.
*He makes an actual note in an actual margin with Raven's actual purple gel pen. He stares at it with something like wonder.*
Mind you, if I'm not a ghost, perhaps nobody is. Perhaps they're all just very committed to a look.
*The radio in the hall crackles: 'BIG STORM SATURDAY. Flooding expected.' Every spore on Malcolm stands up like the fur on a cat.*
Rain. Glorious rain. ...Oh dear. That's bad for you, isn't it. I'm a fungus with a conscience now. It's AWFUL.
*He walks you to the closet door, which is as far as he goes.*
Let me have one last wet weekend, my editor. Then you can fix me. Properly.
*Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like a slammed door. Rain pours through the bedroom ceiling into the closet. You can hear the mold drinking it.*
{player}.
*It's the first time he's said your name. He says it like the first line of a poem he's been revising for weeks.*
Come in. Mind the puddle. The puddle is also me.
*Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like a slammed door. Rain pours through the bedroom ceiling into the closet. You can hear the mold drinking it.*
My editor. Come in. Mind the puddle. The puddle is also me.
*Malcolm is ENORMOUS. The mold has spread up the bedroom wall and across the ceiling toward your bed. He's drunk on damp.*
I am VAST, my dear. I contain [multitudes]. I feel spore-tacular.
*In the hall, Dennis's bucket is full and his little light has gone red. Malcolm has never looked happier.*
*You cough. And cough. You can't stop. The smile falls off Malcolm's face.*
You: Multitudes?
Whitman. Or Raven. She wrote it on her pencil case. I genuinely can't tell my sources apart anymore.
*He's beside you instantly, which at his size means he's also above you, behind you and on the lamp.*
That's me, isn't it. In your chest.
In the novels, the heroine coughs delicately in chapter three and by chapter nine everyone's in black at a windy funeral. I know how this one goes. Love isn't supposed to come with an inhaler.
It has to be tonight, doesn't it. Not Monday. Tonight.
Before you start. Did you hear the podcast this morning? The library. A man died under a sink in 1987.
I SAID that. I said it in 2009. Everyone laughed. The toaster laughed. Well. It didn't. It was dead.

choices.text: You were right about Lukey. He knows now.
I showed Tyler his last video.
Wyatt said no to me. Out loud.
Malcolm. Focus. The closet.

lines: Of course he does. Seventeen years I've been saying it, and he finds out from two retired ladies and a MICROFICHE.
*Through the wall, very faintly, someone is singing Bon Jovi. Malcolm smiles despite himself.*
Give my mold-in-law my regards. He'll hate that.
*His lip curls. Then, surprisingly, uncurls.*
I know. I was in this closet that day. I heard the whole tour. And then I heard the quiet.
Disgusting boy. Ghastly taste. ...Be kind to him. Somebody should finally tell him no and mean it nicely.
He did? OUT LOUD?
*Malcolm presses a fuzzy hand to his chest.*
Good. Good for him. That boy's been swallowing his 'no' since before I was a spore. I hope a certain someone in pink notices one day. ...Never mind. Forget I said that.
*You pull on the respirator and gloves. Malcolm hovers in the closet doorway, wringing his hands. Rain hammers the window.*
Well, then. Here we are. Tell me what to do, my dear. One last time.

choices.text: Hold still and let me take care of you.
No. You tell ME. What do you want?
Get in the bucket, Malcolm.

lines: *He holds still. He doesn't flinch once.*
Take care of me. Yes. Ruin my entire aesthetic.
*He opens his mouth to protest. Closes it. Thinks. Actually thinks.*
I want to stop hurting you. And then maybe a hobby. Pottery. Something with a kiln. Something DRY.
That's my choice. I made it. Nobody wrote it for me. ...Ow. Growth hurts.
*His eyes flutter closed.*
The bucket. You remembered what I like. ...You know this is deeply unhealthy for both of us. I love it.
*You get to work. Cut out the rotten drywall. Bag it. Vacuum. Scrub the studs. Dennis drinks the air. Malcolm narrates like a nature documentary about his own demise.*
*You reach for a spray bottle. Malcolm freezes.*
Is that... BLEACH?

choices.text: No bleach. I promise. Just soap and water.
Hand him the sponge. Let him help.
Tease him: 'Industrial strength.'

lines: *He sags against the doorframe with relief.*
You remembered. Nobody's ever remembered my trauma before. That's the most romantic thing that's ever happened in this closet, and a teenage girl once wrote a Darcy duel in here.
*He takes the sponge and scrubs his own wall, slowly, wearing an expression of enormous suffering.*
Is this what it's like? Doing something good for yourself? It's horrible. I feel incredible. I hate it.
*He screams. A full Victorian scream, both hands to his face.*
*It's dish soap. You show him the label. He doesn't speak to you for four entire minutes, which, for Malcolm, is a silent film.*
*By midnight the closet is bare, scrubbed studs and the storm is easing. Raven's notebooks sit on your bed, sealed in a bag, dry and safe.*
*Malcolm is small now. A pale, dry, soft grey smudge of a man, blinking at the room like he's never seen it before.*
You fixed me. And the character's all still here. The poems. 'Banana.' It was never the rot, was it. It was the stories.

choices.text: It was you. Rot or no rot.
Raven's stories are safe. So are yours.
Told you so.

lines: *He puts a dry, fuzz-free hand on yours. It's still cold. It's warming up.*
Rot or no rot. That's going in the second draft.
Ours. Hers and mine. In an acid-free archival box. I'll write the label myself. In gel pen. Obviously.
*His eyes narrow.*
You did. I hate it. Please never say it again. ...Say it once more. No. Don't.
I can't pass on, my dear. I was never alive. There's no light for me. Just your desk lamp.
And I can't live in a wall anymore. I'm a fungus without a home. Where do I go?

choices.text: Move into a terrarium on my nightstand. I'm in love with you.
I love you. Go somewhere your rot is adored.
Stay as my friend. The kitchen needs a sourdough starter.
That's your call, Malcolm.
That's your call, Malcolm.

lines: *He goes very still. Then all of him (there isn't much of him now) blushes a gentle green.*
A terrarium. A little glass house. On your NIGHTSTAND. Moss. A fern. A tiny ceramic bench.
I'll be a respectable fungus. So respectable. I'll wear a little cap.
*He kisses you. It's cold, a little earthy and very, very sincere.*

v4_rs2.fxText: The closet was finally dry. Nothing else in the bedroom was.
lines: *Much later.*
New poem. It's called 'Dry.' It's one line long: '{player}.' That's it. That's the poem.
*He smiles. It's the softest thing he has ever done with his face.*
You'd let me go to be loved for my rot, rather than keep me and ask me to change. That's the most romantic thing anyone's ever done for a fungus.
There's a cheese cave in Wisconsin. Award-winning blue. I'll finally be cultured.
*He kisses your hand, bows and drifts out of the window into the last of the rain.*
Sourdough. A fungus with a JOB. People would want me. On purpose. With butter.
I accept. I'll need a jar with a dramatic label. ...I knead this. Oh no. Four seconds in the kitchen and I'm already doing Lukey's puns.
*He opens his mouth to beg you to decide. Then he stops.*
My call. Mine. Nobody's written this bit for me.
...Then I choose the kitchen. I'll be a sourdough starter. Useful. Rising. Lukey can keep an eye on me, if he's still dripping about.
Thank you, my dear. For editing me. And for my first ever choice.
My CALL? You scrub me to the studs and won't even tell me where to GO?
Fine. Mrs. Pruitt's garden shed. It's dark, it's damp and nobody there has ever said 'resale.'
*He sweeps out of the window. A wet page flutters onto your bed: a forty-page poem called 'Remediation.' It's the word 'no,' over and over, with feeling.*
We've spoken today, my dear. My quota of human contact is exhausted.
Come back next week. I'll have written something devastating about you.
*On your nightstand, in a little glass terrarium, a very small, very respectable mushroom in a very small cap clears his throat.*
Eleven poems since breakfast. Sit. Listen. That's an order. ...Please. You're better at orders. Give me one.

*A postcard is wedged in the closet doorframe: a cheese cave in Wisconsin. On the back, in gel pen: 'They call me Grand Reserve. I have never been so appreciated. Still yours, in a blue sort of way. M.'*
*The closet is clean and quiet. From the kitchen, very faintly, comes a long, theatrical sigh. The sourdough jar wants feeding, and it wants everyone to know.*
*The closet is clean and dry. Through the window you can see Mrs. Pruitt's shed. There's a black smudge on its door in the shape of a frowning face. It's facing your house. On purpose.*
